title: Relative clauses 5: extra information clauses (2)
subtitle: all of whom / most of which / which was a shame
summary: Use a preposition + whom/which, expressions like all of whom and most of which, and which to refer back to a whole idea.

lesson.heading: preposition + whom / which
lesson.text: In extra information clauses you can put the preposition before **whom** (for people) or **which** (for things): *to whom, with whom, about whom, of which, without which, from which* etc.

examples.text: Mr Lee, **to whom I spoke** at the meeting, is interested in our proposal.
Fortunately we had a good map, **without which** we would have got lost.
The accident, **in which** two people were injured, happened late last night.

lesson.heading: The preposition can stay after the verb
lesson.text: In spoken English we often keep the preposition after the verb. When we do this, we use **who** (not whom) for people.

examples.text: Katherine works for a company called 'Latoma', **which I'd never heard of** before.
Mr Lee, **who I spoke to** at the meeting, is interested in our proposal.
examples.wrong: Mr Lee, whom I spoke to

lesson.heading: all of / most of / none of + whom/which
lesson.text: You can say **all of whom, many of whom, some of whom, neither of whom** etc. for people, and **all of which, none of which, both of which, one of which** etc. for things.

examples.text: Helen has three brothers, **all of whom** are married.
They asked me a lot of questions, **most of which** I couldn't answer.
Martin tried on three jackets, **none of which** fitted him.
Two men, **neither of whom** I had seen before, came into the office.
Sue has a lot of friends, **many of whom** she was at school with.

lesson.heading: the name of which / the cause of which
lesson.text: In the same way you can say **the cause of which**, **the name of which**, **the aim of which** etc.

examples.text: The house was damaged in a fire, **the cause of which** was never established.
We stayed at a beautiful hotel, **the name of which** I don't remember now.

lesson.heading: which for a whole idea
lesson.text: Joe got the job. This surprised everybody. In one sentence: *Joe got the job, **which surprised everybody**.* Here **which** = the fact that Joe got the job. We use **which**, never *what*, in sentences like these.

examples.text: Sarah couldn't meet us, **which was a shame**.
The weather was good, **which we hadn't expected**.
Alex passed his exams, **which is good news**.

lesson.text: When the relative clause comments on the whole sentence before it, always use which - never what.

exercises.prompt: Fortunately we had a good map, ___ we would have got lost.
exercises.explanation: A map is a thing, so after a preposition we use which.

exercises.prompt: The accident, ___ two people were injured, happened late last night.
exercises.explanation: Two people were injured in the accident: in + which.

exercises.prompt: I share an office with my boss, ___ I get on really well.
exercises.explanation: My boss is a person, so after a preposition we use whom.

exercises.prompt: Ben showed me his new car, ___ he's very proud.
exercises.explanation: He is proud of the car - a thing, so of which.

exercises.prompt: Sarah showed us a picture of her son, ___ she's very proud.
exercises.explanation: She is proud of her son - a person, so of whom.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the comment that follows it. Each comment begins with which.

pairs.left: Laura couldn't come to the party,
The street I live in is noisy at night,
pairs.right: which makes it difficult to sleep sometimes.

pairs.left: Kate let me stay at her house,
pairs.right: which was very kind of her.
which makes it hard to contact her.
which means we can't go away tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: All of Helen's brothers are married. Helen has three brothers, ___ are married.
exercises.explanation: For people we say all of whom, not all of which or all of them.

exercises.prompt: Most of the information we were given was useless. We were given a lot of information, ___ useless.
exercises.explanation: Information is a thing, so we use most of which.

exercises.prompt: James won a lot of money and he gave half of it to his parents. Make one sentence.
exercises.answer: James won a lot of money, half of which he gave to his parents
exercises.explanation: Half of which refers back to the money.

exercises.prompt: We stayed at a very nice hotel, ___ I don't remember.
exercises.explanation: We say the name of which / the cause of which / the aim of which.

exercises.statement: Sarah couldn't meet us, what was a shame.
exercises.explanation: Sarah couldn't meet us, which was a shame. We use which, not what, to refer back to a whole idea.

exercises.prompt: Mr Lee, ___ I spoke to at the meeting, is interested in our proposal.
exercises.explanation: When the preposition stays after the verb (spoke to), we use who, not whom.
